Task 4: Energy Savings Verification Following the data management plan, staff collected, stored, and analyzed energy use and maintenance data before and after retrofits. Data collection began in June 2024. Over 11 months, NREL gathered utility bills to compare with data from previous years, including from the original energy audits. Building use and occupancy changed over the project’s period of performance, which spanned the COVID-19 pandemic; this introduced some uncertainty into the energy savings analysis. However, the data show that compared with the building performance during and just before the energy audits, the Tribal Office saw energy reductions by about 26% EUI. 4.1 Collect data: Utility bills (electricity and #1 Heating Oil) were collected for the Office building. All data were stored in a secure location. 4.2 Analyze data: Staff analyzed the data to evaluate potential changes in building performance and energy consumption, and results were presented in both graphical and written formats. For this TA effort, utility bills for electricity and fuel oil usage were supplied by ANC employees and the utility for the calendar years 2023 through March 2025. Actual and modeled data used in the 2017 energy audit were obtained from the energy auditor. Task 5: Outreach ANC presented annual updates at the OIE Program Review each November (2022, 2023, 2024). NREL assisted with presentation slides; NREL also created a poster/flyer for information dissemination once the project was completed. 6 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 5.0 Methods NREL staff reviewed construction documents and compiled the utility data to calculate annual energy usage metrics for the Tribal Office building. Monthly utility bills for fuel oil and electricity were collected for three distinct periods: before the retrofits, during the baseline assessment period, and after the retrofits were in place. Pre-retrofit data were derived from the original energy audit and recent utility records to establish a baseline of energy consumption before any upgrades. Post-retrofit utility data were collected in the years following implementation to evaluate performance under comparable climatic conditions. Energy use intensity (EUI) was reported in terms of annual kBtu/ft² (thousand British thermal units per square foot2) for each full calendar year of available data. EUI is defined as the total annual energy consumption normalized by the conditioned floor area of the building, providing a standardized metric for comparing energy consumption across years; the higher the EUI, the less efficient the building.
